reference.title: Dumbbell One Arm Bench Fly
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Chest, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the arm opens, exhale as you sweep it back up.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, 0.4 s stretch, 1.5 s up

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9). Use a lighter dumbbell than for a two-arm fly at first.
prescription.progression: More reps, a longer pause in the stretch, then the next dumbbell.

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench, feet planted wide; hold one dumbbell over the chest, palm facing in, elbow softly bent; rest the other hand on your stomach.
Breathe in and open the arm in a wide arc, elbow bend fixed, hips and shoulders staying flat.
Stop with the upper arm about level with the bench, palm to the ceiling, chest stretched.
Breathe out and sweep the dumbbell back up along the same arc, squeezing the chest.
Dumbbell back over the chest, the trunk still square; repeat, then switch sides.

mistakes.fix: Brace, plant both feet wide and keep both shoulder blades on the bench.
Keep the same soft elbow bend all the way down and up.
Stop with the upper arm about level with the bench.
Keep a soft bend (elbow about 150-160 degrees).
Lower slowly and pause briefly at the bottom.

kinematics.norm: Fixed soft bend: Solstad 2020 held the elbow at about 150-160 degrees (20-30 degrees of flexion) in the fly
From over the chest to about level with the bench (clinical opinion)
Upper arm about level with the bench at the bottom, no lower (clinical opinion)
Rests on the stomach (clinical opinion; the GymVisual reference is used only to identify the movement)
Feet flat and a little wider than for a two-arm fly for a stable base, knees about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Slow and controlled, about 2-3 s down and 1.5-2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #128512, Dumbbell One Arm Bench Fly, video (movement reference)

Solstad, Andersen, Shaw, Hoel, Vonheim and Saeterbakken 2020, a comparison of muscle activation between barbell bench press and dumbbell flyes in resistance-trained males (J Sports Sci Med 19(4):645-651; PMC7675616)

Patterson, Vigotsky, Oppenheimer and Feser 2015, differences in unilateral chest press muscle activation and kinematics on a stable versus unstable surface while holding one versus two dumbbells (PeerJ 3:e1365; PMC4627906)

cautions: Get into position with the dumbbell on the thigh, lie back and bring it up over the chest; at the end lower it back to the thigh or the floor beside the bench (clinical opinion).
Do not let the dumbbell pull the arm below the bench line: the stretched shoulder is the vulnerable position (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms; bent-back wrists under a heavy dumbbell strain the wrist.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Rolling off balance: hold the bench edge with the free hand.
regressions: Two-arm dumbbell fly with light dumbbells.
Floor fly (the floor limits the depth).
progressions: Single-arm fly on a bench with the feet together (more trunk demand).

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main mover: hugs the working arm across the chest (horizontal adduction). In the two-arm fly pectoralis activity was about 16% below the barbell bench press overall (Solstad 2020); holding one dumbbell instead of two did not change pectoralis activity in a unilateral press (Patterson 2015).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Helps bring the arm in; about 25% lower than in the bench press in the two-arm fly (Solstad 2020).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Holds the fixed elbow bend against the load: much higher than in the bench press in the fly (Solstad 2020).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blade on the rib cage.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: steadies the shoulder in the stretched position (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the pull of the single dumbbell rolling the trunk toward the working side (clinical opinion; oblique activity changed across one- and two-dumbbell conditions in Patterson 2015).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the pull of the single dumbbell rolling the trunk toward the working side (clinical opinion; oblique activity changed across one- and two-dumbbell conditions in Patterson 2015).
muscleNotes.core: Brace so the hips and shoulders stay square on the bench.
